title: Côte d'Ivoire, the world's largest cocoa producer, is moving towards the privatization of its cocoa and coffee marketing, a decision prompted by the IMF and World Bank. This shift has raised concerns among foreign buyers regarding the potential impact on the quantity and quality of cocoa supplies. Currently, the state-run Cocoa marketing board, Caistab, controls the marketing and pricing of cocoa, but with liberalization set to begin in October 1999, there are fears that the transition could disrupt forward contract sales, which have been a reliable method for securing cocoa supplies. Experts predict that many of the newly licensed private exporters may struggle to meet the demands of the market, leading to uncertainty in the global cocoa market. The situation is reminiscent of past liberalizations in Nigeria and Cameroon, which resulted in a decline in forward sales. As Côte d'Ivoire prepares for this significant change, both local farmers and international buyers are bracing for the potential upheaval in the cocoa industry.
